# Getting an image {#sec-getting-an-image}

This chapter gives one recipe for each kind of image you can take by hand:
a still image, a bioluminescence image, a composite, a video and a Z-stack.
The controls the recipes use are described in @sec-channels and
@sec-focus, and the toolbar's buttons in @sec-toolbar. To take images
automatically, at many positions or over time, use a protocol
(@sec-protocols).

## Before you capture {#sec-image-before}

- Place the sample on the stage: a microplate directly in the nest, other
  labware in the universal labware holder (@sec-labware-holders).
- Make sure LumaViewPro knows which objective is in the light path
  (@sec-objective). It won't capture until it does.
- Choose a destination folder with the toolbar's Destination folder
  button. Every image and video you take is saved inside it
  (@sec-image-files).
- Choose the file format in [Live Image Format]{.guilabel} (@sec-live-format)
  and the bit depth in [Image Mode]{.guilabel}
  (@sec-image-mode), both in [Microscope Settings]{.guilabel}.

## A still image {#sec-image-still}

For a transmitted-light or fluorescence channel:

1. If your Lumascope has a motorized stage, move to the sample, or to the
   first well of a plate: click its spot on the plate map in
   [XY Stage Control]{.guilabel} (@sec-plate-map), or right-click a point
   in the live image to center it (@sec-click-to-center).
2. Open the channel's drawer in the right panel, for example
   [Brightfield]{.channel}. The live image switches to that channel.
3. Turn on [Enable LED]{.guilabel}.
4. Focus until the sample is sharp (@sec-focus-adjust). Once it's close,
   [Autofocus]{.guilabel} can finish the job (@sec-autofocus).
5. Adjust [LED (mA)]{.guilabel}, [Gain (dB)]{.guilabel} and
   [Exp (ms)]{.guilabel} until the image is bright but not saturated. Most
   of the histogram (@sec-histogram) should sit away from both ends.
6. If your Lumascope has a focus motor, click [Save Focus]{.guilabel} to
   keep this focus for the channel (@sec-channel-focus). To return to this
   spot later, click [Set Z]{.guilabel} in [Objective Control]{.guilabel},
   plus [Set X]{.guilabel} and [Set Y]{.guilabel} in
   [XY Stage Control]{.guilabel} if you have a motorized stage.
7. Click Capture in the toolbar.

The image is saved in the `Manual` folder inside your destination folder.
Its name includes the channel and a number that goes up with each
capture, such as `live_BF_000001.tiff`. With a motorized stage, the well
is included too: `live_D6_BF_000001.tiff`. TIFF and OME-TIFF files store
the channel, LED current, gain, exposure, objective and stage position
with the image; JPG files don't (@sec-live-format).

Capture always takes a new image from the camera. If the LED is off,
you'll get a dark image, so check [Enable LED]{.guilabel} first. Freeze
only pauses the display; Capture still saves a new image from the camera,
not the frozen one.

If LumaViewPro doesn't know where the stage is, for example before it has
homed, the image is saved without a well or position, and you'll see a
"Position Not Recorded" message. Click [Home Stage]{.guilabel}, and later
images will include them.

## A bioluminescence image {#sec-image-lumi}

*[Lumi]{.channel} channel only.*

A luminescent sample is often too faint to focus by its own light, so
focus in a transmitted-light channel first:

1. Open the [Brightfield]{.channel} or [Phase Contrast]{.channel} drawer,
   turn on [Enable LED]{.guilabel}, focus on the sample, and click
   [Save Focus]{.guilabel}.
2. Open the [Lumi]{.channel} drawer. [Lumi]{.channel} has no LED; the
   camera images the light the sample gives off.
3. Raise [Gain (dB)]{.guilabel} and [Exp (ms)]{.guilabel} toward the top
   of their ranges.
4. If the live image still shows nothing, set [Sum]{.guilabel} to add
   several frames into each image, for example 4 (@sec-sum). The extra
   range from summing is kept only in a full-depth
   [Image Mode]{.guilabel}.
5. Click Capture in the toolbar. Then click Open last save folder in the
   toolbar, open the image, and check that the luminescence shows.

To image [Lumi]{.channel} at the focus you found in transmitted light,
click [Save Focus]{.guilabel} in the [Lumi]{.channel} drawer too, before
you move the focus.

## A composite image {#sec-image-composite}

A composite combines several channels of the same field into one image:
fluorescence channels layered over each other, or over one
transmitted-light channel.

1. Set up and focus each channel as for a still image, and in each
   channel's drawer set [Acquire Settings]{.guilabel} to
   [Image]{.guilabel} (@sec-channel-acquire). You need at least two
   channels set to [Image]{.guilabel}; with fewer, LumaViewPro won't make
   the composite and shows "Not Enough Channels".
2. For each fluorescence or [Lumi]{.channel} channel, set
   [CBT (%)]{.guilabel}. Pixels brighter than this are laid over the
   transmitted-light image (@sec-cbt).
3. Click Composite in the toolbar. Each channel is captured in turn with
   its own settings, at its saved focus. A channel with no saved focus
   uses the current focus, and a channel with [Auto Focus]{.guilabel} on
   autofocuses first. A composite finishes by itself; to interrupt it,
   click Composite again. The channels already captured are kept, but no
   combined image is made.

Each composite gets its own folder, `Manual/Composites/<date>_<time>/`,
inside your destination folder. It holds one image per channel, such as
`Composite_BF_0000.tiff`, and the combined image in a `Composite`
subfolder. Composites are saved as TIFF or OME-TIFF
(@sec-sequenced-format). The per-channel images keep the bit depth set in
[Image Mode]{.guilabel} (@sec-image-mode); the combined image is 8-bit
color.

## A video {#sec-image-video}

1. Set up and focus the channel as for a still image.
2. Click Record in the toolbar, and click it again to stop. If you don't,
   recording stops at [Video Time Limit (s)]{.guilabel}: 300 seconds
   unless you change it in [Advanced Settings]{.guilabel}
   (@sec-advanced-camera).

The video is saved in the `Manual` folder, named with the date and time it
started, such as `Video_2026-11-04_21.28.29.mp4`. The name doesn't include
the channel; a file next to it ending in `_manifest.json` records the
channel and the frames written. With [Video Recording Format]{.guilabel}
set to [Frames]{.guilabel}, the frames are saved as separate images in a
folder with that name instead (@sec-video-format).

## A Z-stack {#sec-image-zstack}

*Motorized focus only.*

1. Set up the channel as for a still image, and focus at the depth you
   want as the top, center or bottom of the stack.
2. In [Objective Control]{.guilabel}, under [Acquire Z Stack]{.guilabel},
   set the step size, the range, and where the stack sits relative to the
   current focus (@sec-zstack).
3. Click [Acquire]{.guilabel}.

The slices are saved in a new folder, `Manual/Z-Stacks/<date>_<time>/`.

## Where your images go {#sec-image-files}

Everything is saved inside the destination folder. Each folder below is
created the first time something is saved to it.

| Folder | What it holds |
|:---|:---|
| `Manual` | Still images and videos taken with Capture and Record. |
| `Manual/Composites/<date>_<time>` | One folder for each composite. |
| `Manual/Z-Stacks/<date>_<time>` | One folder for each Z-stack. |
| `ProtocolData/<date>_<time>` | One folder for each protocol run. |

: The folders under the destination folder {#tbl-image-folders tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

If [Save channels in separate folders]{.guilabel} is on in
[Advanced Settings]{.guilabel} (@sec-advanced-protocol), still images go
into a folder per channel inside `Manual`, such as `Manual/BF`.

Open last save folder in the toolbar opens the folder LumaViewPro saved to
most recently.
